title: Route on in-flight load, not request count
lesson: Round robin rotates through replicas without measuring request cost. This illustrative schedule shows a small request waiting while another replica is idle; selecting a minimum in-flight count avoids that placement for later new requests. The count remains an imperfect proxy for work.
limitations: Illustrative single-execution-slot model: token sizes and 6 s / 0.6 s service times are invented. The elapsed badges are calculated from scene send/receive times, including animated transport; they are not benchmark results or guaranteed token runtimes. The two phases are different schedules, not a controlled performance replay.

The in-flight count is a proxy for load, not a measure of work (the Google SRE chapter's own caveat): two replicas with equal counts can hold very different work. Least in-flight cannot tell them apart; the cut shows it helping only after short requests finish and the counts diverge. Weighted or utilisation-based policies, health checks, connection draining and long-lived connections are not shown; the baseline cut covers health checks.

The policy label changing on the balancer is a scene event. Routing policy is configuration enforced by the balancer or client library; a label, prompt or persistent instruction does not enforce routing, and by the same token persistent prompts do not enforce permissions.

The orange second slot and WAIT badge represent a local waiting request, not parallel execution. Its bar stays empty until execution starts. In-flight counters count backend-arrived, unfinished work; transport and response travel are excluded from this toy signal.
Decoded audio peak -1.2 dBFS; all 107 scheduled 160 ms cue windows contain energy. Waveform and spectrogram were analysed; overlapping cues were not isolated and audio was not heard.
transcript: 0:00.7–0:05.7 — Normal case under ROUND ROBIN. Three small '2k tokens' requests leave the client about a second apart. The balancer's pointer steps to Replica 1, 2 and 3 in turn; each replica's counter ticks to '1 in flight' and back to 0 as its slot finishes, and each response returns with a green '2.8 s' demo-elapsed badge. The footer marks the schedule illustrative; all badges measure animation elapsed time, not production latency.

0:07.3–0:12.0 — Costs diverge. A '60k tokens' request lands on Replica 1 and another on Replica 2; their slots fill slowly with a low ticking. A small request lands on Replica 3 and finishes after 0.6 s of service. At 0:11.4 the three counters pop together: every replica has had exactly one request, yet they read 1, 1 and 0 because the short one is done.

0:12.2–0:16.7 — The misroute. The next small request leaves and the rotation points at Replica 1 anyway. It lands at 0:13.5 with a buzz and a jolt; Replica 1's counter turns orange at '2 in flight' and the request waits in an empty second slot with a WAIT badge until 0:15.25; it then starts filling with an arrival cue. Replica 3's counter ripples green at 0:14.0 to show it was free. The heavy jobs finish and return grey envelopes; the delayed small response arrives last at 0:16.65 with an orange '4.5 s' demo-elapsed badge.

0:18.0–0:19.3 — The fix. The balancer flashes green and its label changes in place to LEAST IN-FLIGHT; three green dots run from the counters up to the balancer's ports and a chime confirms the counters are now inputs.

0:19.8–0:26.8 — Resolution. The first heavy request is selected while all counters are 0; rotation breaks the tie toward Replica 2. By the next selection Replica 2 has one unfinished call, so the remaining zero-count tie selects Replica 3. With the counters at 0, 1, 1 the next small request goes to Replica 1 (its counter flashes green at the pick) and returns with a '2.8 s' demo-elapsed badge at 0:24.6; the one after that goes to Replica 1 again, where round robin would have sent it to busy Replica 2, and returns with a '2.8 s' demo-elapsed badge at 0:26.75.
0:27.0–0:31.8 — The heavy jobs complete and all counters return to 0 under the LEAST IN-FLIGHT label; the stage holds, then fades to the title-only frame that also opens the video.

corrections.change: Replace arbitrary response-time badges with elapsed client-send-to-client-receive times from the toy schedule (2.8 s clear, 4.5 s delayed), label demo elapsed and mark the example illustrative.
Show an explicit WAIT badge and zero progress on the queued slot; clear WAIT and sound the execution start.
Enlarge the policy subtitle to 36px and widen its box.
Fresh canvas per captured frame, software rendering and synchronous pixel readback prevent missing title/node rasters reproduced at 15.3s and 17.2s during preflight.
